newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia, Japan set up task force on trade deficit.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia, Japan set up task force on trade deficit.

text.p: Malaysia and Japan have set up a task force to address the chronic trade deficit that Malaysia has with Japan, Malaysia's International Trade and Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz said on Tuesday.

The task force was agreed upon in talks between Malaysia's Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad and Japanese premier Ryutaro Hashimoto during the latter's visit last month, the national news agency Bernama quoted Rafidah as saying.

Japan would be represented by Trade and Industry International Economic Affairs director general Kazamasa Kusaka and Malaysia by Ministry of International Trade and Industry secretary-general Asmat Kamaluddin, Rafidah said.
The task force would seek positive approaches to solving the trade deficit problem, she said.
This was the first time such a task force was formed on a bilateral basis. Previous approaches had been tackled at a regional level, Rafidah said.
Malaysia says its trade deficit with Japan narrowed to 4.5 billion ringgit in the first 10 months of 1996 from 29.5 billion in all of 1995.
According to the Japanese embassy in Kuala Lumpur, the trade deficit with Malaysia for all of 1996 declined by one third to 390.27 billion yen. It did not give figures for 1995.
